title: Writing for Guy Hall, the Book-Cadillac band and law school doubts
summary: He left Harman, arranged for local bands, sent a semiclassical arrangement to Detroit, and debated law school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: -- writing an arrangement and you were going to go to Penn law school.

I had that in mind in the fall. Now, this was some time during the winter that I was with the Harmán band. Something developed there, anyway, I left him and went back to my hometown, Wilkes Barre, and I played around with Guy Hall, with local bands, made some arrangements for them, just to -- you know, they were busy and I was making a little bit of money, but as I said, one of the reasons I wanted to go to law school, because I didn't want to sit around Wilkes Barre being a musician and I didn't know where to get to a bigger band, or to -- I thought, 'Well, this is not for me, the music business. I had better quit while I'm ahead and I am

prepared to go to law school," so now there must have been three, four months, maybe five months during that winter or spring and summer before I would decide to do this, to go away. At which time I went back to Wilkes Barre and I think, I made the arrangement of something -- I think it was something semi-classical. Anyway it was something that they didn't want as I know the Goldkette band now, so they sent it down to the Book, for the other band.
So I didn't pay too much attention. I didn't hear from them that they wanted more.
How much did you get paid for that?

I don't know. I think I got about 50 bucks. Maybe 25. I don't remember, but anyway I am busy around there and the idea of going to Penn was beginning to jell. I played around there during the summer and one time during -- towards the end of the summer, I am hearing that the Goldkette band is going to come through. I told a friend of mine who I played with, I said, "look, I made that arrangement for them. I don't know if they've played it." Let's see, in the meantime they had -- yes, I must have heard from them, because they had asked me to do another arrangement, an arrangement of "Baby Face."
